Object editor

The shared editor that opens any FortiWeb configuration object with its sub-tables, previews every change as a dry run and writes it to the device only when you confirm.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view network.edit network.apply protection.edit operations.template_save
📍 WhereOpened from the FortiWeb device menu pages (the pencil beside a reference selector, and Create New where FortiWeb's layout has none), the configuration section pages and reference fields (URL /objedit/<appliance id>/edit?collection=<collection>&mkey=<name>)

What is it?#

The object editor is the one form SATOM uses to edit any FortiWeb configuration object. It shows the object's own fields grouped like the FortiWeb GUI, and below them every sub-table the object owns (pool members, virtual-IP lists, host lists, match conditions, rules…), each row editable in place. Every change is previewed as a dry run first and written to the device only when you click Apply to device.

What does it do?#

  • Renders fields with the widget FortiWeb uses: on/off toggles, drop-down lists, number boxes, text boxes and reference drop-downs that list the objects configured on the device.
  • Hides fields that do not apply to the current selection (for example fields that depend on a mode), and never sends their values.
  • Lets you open a referenced object (✎ or ↗) or create a new one (＋) in a panel that slides in from the right, stacked over the current page.
  • Edits sub-table rows one by one: Save row, Delete, and ＋ Add row → Create row.
  • Shows a Changes vs local source of truth table (field, before, after) and the exact REST request before anything is written.
  • Checks reference values and delete references against the device before writing (see Troubleshooting).
  • Falls back to SATOM's local copy when the device does not answer, so the object stays visible.
  • Shows a short description of the object type, its device behaviour and a FortiWeb admin guide ↗ link when SATOM has one, and explains what each Action value does under the drop-down.
  • Offers a regex tester (.* button) next to fields that take a regular expression.

Requirements#

  • The appliance must be visible to you (current ADOM, not in maintenance unless you may see maintenance devices).
  • The object type must exist in SATOM's endpoint registry. Any other value shows Unknown object type.

Permissions#

Action Required
Open an object, read reference lists protection.view
Save fields, create, save/delete rows, delete, clone Configuration write — any of network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit, protection.apply, operations.apply, appliances.edit, appliances.apply or an operations.template_* key
Save as template (Configuration sections only) operations.template_save

Without write permission the buttons are still shown; the request is refused and the result box shows Forbidden.

How to use#

Change an object's fields#

  1. Open the object (for example Edit on a Server Objects row).
  2. Expand a field group under Settings and change the values.
  3. Click Review & save. If nothing changed you see No changes to save.
  4. Check the preview: the changed fields with their before/after values, the HTTP method and path, and the request body.
  5. Click Apply to device. Applied to device. confirms the write and the page reloads.

Fields the build lacks, and fields only the CLI serves#

Every save is also checked against the appliance's exact firmware build (Build compatibility). The preview shows the result above the request:

  • a field the build does not have is skipped (removed from the write) and named — FortiWeb would otherwise answer 200 and drop it; if every changed field is missing, the save is refused;
  • a value the build does not accept, or an object it does not have, is refused on apply: Refused by the build compatibility check: …;
  • a build SATOM never measured reads not measured — cannot be guaranteed.

A field the build serves only by CLI is written by the CLI writer: the preview shows the CLI script, the apply sends REST first and then the script, and Readback (CLI) / Readback (REST) stay on screen instead of the page reloading. FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 have no CLI-only field, so on those builds everything still goes by REST.

Create an object#

  1. Click New on a list page (or ＋ beside a reference field).
  2. Enter Name (the object's unique key) and any initial fields.
  3. Click Review & create, then Create on device.
  4. Created. Opening editor… — the editor switches to the new object so you can add its sub-table rows.

Some types need more than a name: a custom Service needs Port, a Virtual IP needs IP / Netmask. The create is refused with <field> required for this object type until you fill it in.

Edit sub-table rows#

  1. Under the sub-table card (N row(s) · <segment>), expand a row.
  2. Change it and click Save row, or click Delete (confirm Delete this row?).
  3. To add a row, expand ＋ Add row, fill in the fields and click Create row.
  4. Each action previews first; click Apply to device to write it.

Work with referenced objects#

  • Pick a value from a reference drop-down. The list is filled from the device (or from the local copy when the device does not answer).
  • ✎ opens the selected object in a slide-over panel; ＋ opens a create form in a panel. Creating there selects the new name in the drop-down that opened it. Press Esc to close the top panel.
  • ＋ is not offered for interfaces or for certificate stores that can only be imported.

Clone or delete an object#

Delete is offered on the list pages (two confirmations, dry run first). Clone is offered on the Web Protection pages: it reads the source object and its sub-table rows from the device, previews a plan (object, new_name, number of rows) and, when applied, creates the copy and then its rows under the new name.

Configuration#

Element Description Required Example
Name Unique key of a new object. Shown only in create mode. Yes (create) pool-shop
Settings groups The object's scalar fields, grouped as in the FortiWeb GUI. Only changed fields are sent. — lb-algo
Reference drop-down Names an object that must exist on the device. — none — clears it. Depends on the field hc-http
Sub-table card One card per owned sub-table, e.g. pool members. — pserver-list

Example#

🧪Example — Swap the health check of a pool on fweb-01

  1. Open the server policy that uses pool-shop (FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy, Edit) and click the pencil beside Server Pool: the object editor opens pool-shop in a panel stacked over the dialog.
  2. In Settings pick hc-https in the health-check drop-down.
  3. Review & save lists the health-check field with hc-http under Before and hc-https under After, followed by the PUT request to the pool.
  4. Apply to device → Applied to device.

Result#

  • Each applied write goes through SATOM's audited write path: a change-history record with the before/after values and an audit entry (config.create, config.update or config.delete). Previews are not recorded.
  • Applied updates and deletes update SATOM's local copy of the object and release the edit lock.
  • Changing a server policy's web protection profile from this editor marks the policy's authored exceptions as stale (see Exceptions).

Troubleshooting#

"Forbidden"#

Possible causes - Your profile lacks configuration-write permission.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator for one of the keys in Permissions.

": "" — …"#

Possible causes - A reference field names an object the device does not have. FortiWeb would reject the whole save with errcode -651: Invalid input value, so SATOM checks first — on the preview as well as on the apply — and writes nothing.

Solution 1. Pick a value from the drop-down or create the referenced object first. 2. Save again.

Verification - The preview appears instead of the message. If the device could not be asked, the save is not blocked; the response lists the unverified fields.

"refusing to delete "": it is referenced by N object(s) — …"#

Possible causes - Other objects still point at the one you are deleting.

Solution 1. Remove the references named in the message, then delete again.

A variant says the device reports references but does not name them; another says the object could not be read back, so SATOM could not check — in both cases nothing is deleted. Deleting a sub-table row is not checked.

""" is a template-managed profile. Edit it in Administrator → Template Library — …"#

Possible causes - The web protection profile is governed by an approved template and is read-only on device pages.

Solution 1. Edit the template in the Template library instead. Approving it deploys the change to all devices.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: this message used to point at a non-existent "Administrator → WPP Templates" menu; it now names Administrator → Template Library.

"Showing locally cached data (…)"#

The device did not answer the live read (offline or license-locked). The fields stay editable and Apply to device still writes to the device.

"🔒 Being edited by . Saving is blocked to avoid a conflict."#

Possible causes - Another user holds the edit lock on this object.

Solution 1. Wait, or click Take over. See Locks.

If you see Your edit lock was lost (expired or taken). Reload before saving., click Reload before saving.

"No field template is known for this sub-table yet …"#

Solution 1. Run a rediscovery or deep capture of a device that already has rows in this sub-table, then reopen the editor.

Other messages#

  • name required, object name required, row id required, parent object required — the request lacked the identifying value; reopen the object from its list page.
  • new name must differ from the source — choose another clone name.
  • device read failed: … (clone) — the device could not be read; nothing was created.
  • N sub-table row(s) failed to copy — the clone object exists but some rows were not copied; add them manually.

Advanced#

Advanced How sub-tables are found and read

Sub-tables are derived from the endpoint registry: a collection owns every registry path shaped <collection>/<segment>. Rows are always read scoped to the parent (?mkey=<parent>); path-style reads can return every parent's rows. The NTP server list is the one exception — it hangs off a singleton and has no per-row delete, so editing or removing a row rebuilds the whole list and puts the original rows back if a re-add fails.

Advanced Writes

collection is always checked against the registry allow-list (endpoint not allowed otherwise). Writes default to a dry run; only a request carrying apply touches the device. The delete endpoint accepts force to override a reference count the firmware got wrong; forced deletes are audited with ref_check=forced. The edit lock (heartbeat every 30 s) is taken on the full editor page; the inline editor used in Configuration sections and the slide-over panels do not take it.
